text:
ConocoPhillips dropped 1.2% today after jumping 3.1% yesterday, as oil prices retreated on news that the U.S. is considering sanctions relief on Russian crude exports. The market had bid up energy stocks sharply Friday (October 16th) when Iran's attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz pushed crude toward $110 a barrel; today's slide reflects a reversal of that geopolitical premium as potential Russian supply returning to markets could ease the global shortage that had tightened prices.

The stock's two-week gain of 12.7% still reflects a genuinely tight physical oil market—tanker rates have spiked so much that the true delivered cost of crude is roughly $38 to $40 higher than the headline price suggests—but today's move shows investors are trading on the possibility of near-term relief, not the underlying supply constraint.
